# Ketchup

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="ketchup-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="ketchup-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="ketchup-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Ketchup in the HMI library has 120 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn and V from 8 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Oladapo FO, Awokoya JO, Egbedeyi TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals">COMPARATIVE RISK ASSESSMENT OF SOME TOXIC ELEMENTS&#39; CONTENTS IN DOMESTIC AND IMPORTED TOMATO PASTES AND KETCHUP IN NIGERIAN MARKETS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">J. <ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury and nickel and others, in 120 results from 8 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Oladapo FO, Awokoya JO, Egbedeyi TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals">COMPARATIVE RISK ASSESSMENT OF SOME TOXIC ELEMENTS&#39; CONTENTS IN DOMESTIC AND IMPORTED TOMATO PASTES AND KETCHUP IN NIGERIAN MARKETS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">J. Chem. Soc. Nigeria, Vol. 48, No. 3, pp 530-543 [2023]</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Ketchup, as sold from plastic-packed, 4 brands x 3 production series, Iranian market had lead higher at 540 µg/kg, against 510 µg/kg for all packaging types, Iranian market in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Oladapo FO, Awokoya JO, Egbedeyi TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals">COMPARATIVE RISK ASSESSMENT OF SOME TOXIC ELEMENTS&#39; CONTENTS IN DOMESTIC AND IMPORTED TOMATO PASTES AND KETCHUP IN NIGERIAN MARKETS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">J. Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/vaishali2020-tomato-ketchup-delhi-ncr-pb-cd">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, 2 studies with the basis not stated reported means and medians from 23 µg/kg (Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) 2013) to 37.2 µg/kg (Dabeka et al. 1995).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Higher results came from contaminated or exposed settings rather than ordinary supply. Ketchup, as sold from sachet-packed, 4 brands x 3 production series, Iranian market had aluminium higher at 1,700 µg/kg, against 1,380 µg/kg for all packaging types, Iranian market in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the ketchup came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-ketchup" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-ketchup-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of ketchup, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:ketchup-e18b5ff3271a:873fcee1a47d"><summary>HMI ketchup Pb reference · Ketchup, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:ketchup-e18b5ff3271a:873fcee1a47d"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI ketchup Pb reference · Ketchup, as sold. Ketchup, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤4</td><td>5.9–13.7 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤4</td><td>6.24–18 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>37 reference units; 2 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>34</td><td>50%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>50%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for ketchup, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:ketchup-e18b5ff3271a:873fcee1a47d</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for ketchup, as sold on this basis in the completed ketchup ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. ## How metals reach ketchup

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach ketchup comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Ketchup, as sold from sachet-packed, 4 brands x 3 production series, Iranian market had aluminium higher at 1,700 µg/kg, against 1,380 µg/kg for all packaging types, Iranian market in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in ketchup?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn and V in ketchup, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Oladapo FO, Awokoya JO, Egbedeyi TD · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals">COMPARATIVE RISK ASSESSMENT OF SOME TOXIC ELEMENTS&#39; CONTENTS IN DOMESTIC AND IMPORTED TOMATO PASTES AND KETCHUP IN NIGERIAN MARKETS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">J. Chem. Soc. Nigeria, Vol. 48, No. 3, pp 530-543 [2023]</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/oladapo2023-nigeria-tomato-paste-ketchup-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in ketchup, as sold from 197 results in 5 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 1.6 to 21.5 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-ketchup" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-ketchup" data-question="How do heavy metals get into ketchup?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into ketchup?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, ketchup from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than ketchup from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ketchup, as sold from plastic-packed, 4 brands x 3 production series, Iranian market had lead higher at 540 µg/kg, against 510 µg/kg for all packaging types, Iranian market in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Torkashvand J, Torkashvand S, Tamjidi F · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports (Article in Press, accepted 29 September 2026)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/torkashvand2026-iran-sauces-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-ketchup" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-ketchup" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in ketchup?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in ketchup?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, ketchup, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (1.6 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (21.5 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in EURO (7 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (21.5 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-ketchup" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-ketchup" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in ketchup?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in ketchup?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same ketchup.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ketchup, canned (5 city composites) had lead higher at 48.9 µg/kg, against 8.1 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (ketchup, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dabeka RW, McKenzie AD · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Survey of Lead, Cadmium, Fluoride, Nickel, and Cobalt in Food Composites and Estimation of Dietary Intakes of These Elements by Canadians in 1986-1988</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of AOAC International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dabeka1995-canadian-food-composites-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-ketchup-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-ketchup-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in ketchup is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in ketchup is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 2 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR 2012 reported inorganic arsenic at 7 µg/kg (mean) in ketchup, as sold from all samples (4 sampling occasions, composites).<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span
